content.text: This seems like a problem in the way that header is handled in the PrincipalProvider implementations- is there a way we could move the relevant checks into the appropriate classes rather than locating them in the client code?

Benjamin, I'm new to fedora internals and don't follow what you mean by "client code". If you mean moving the checks from ServletContainerAuthenticationProvider into the concrete implementations, I'm all for it - it would help me with better implementation of feature from
- passing groups with on-behalf-of, which we need for our repository instance.
I've sketched one possible solution, see the pseudouml. Comments?
is working on a revised PR for this ticket.
Scenario: both normal users (as configured in tomcat) and impersonated users (via admin account and on-behalf-of header) access the repository.

If admin user calls fedora with on-behalf-of header, all works as expected. If non-admin user calls fedora and adds on-behalf-of header, the contents of header gets propagated to FEDORA_ALL_PRINCIPALS - this is done in HttpHeaderPrincipalProvider.getPrincipals() as DelegateHeaderPrincipalProvider is a subclass of HttpHeader...

comments.body: This seems like a problem in the way that header is handled in the PrincipalProvider implementations- is there a way we could move the relevant checks into the appropriate classes rather than locating them in the client code?

Benjamin, I'm new to fedora internals and don't follow what you mean by "client code". If you mean moving the checks from ServletContainerAuthenticationProvider into the concrete implementations, I'm all for it - it would help me with better implementation of feature from https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/fedora-tech/gcnp6sz1O00 - passing groups with on-behalf-of, which we need for our repository instance.

I've sketched one possible solution, see the pseudouml. Comments? fedora auth.pdf

Thanks, ms.
I believe Benjamin Armintor is working on a revised PR for this ticket.
Benjamin Armintor, any updates?
